correctness.rationale: PASS: The Markov W1 Lipschitz norm equals its maximum adjacent Dirac-pair ratio by coupling convexity and graph geodesics; cycle translation symmetry reduces it to W1(p,shift p). The known circular transport-flow identity reduces to median absolute deviation of the N heat-kernel entries. Reflection symmetry and a positive irreducible Metzler difference system give strictly radial descending entries for all t>0; shell counts give median at r=floor((N+1)/4). Expansion of the heat kernel by shortest-path length with positive coefficients in the defect yields k=floor((N+2)/4), coefficients 2/1/4/3 according to N mod4, including N=3/4/6. Submultiplicativity gives strict decrease; Fourier first eigenspace yields the stated long-time prefactor. Independent matrix exponentials for N=3..22 and t=0.02,0.1,0.7 confirmed median formula and short-time orders. Those finite checks are corroboration, while the proof is all N≥3.

final_claim: For unnormalized continuous-time nearest-neighbor heat semigroup on C_N, all-time W1 Lipschitz norm equals the sum of deviations of the heat kernel from its radial median; first nonzero short-time defect has order floor((N+2)/4) with exact mod-four coefficient, despite strict t>0 contraction.
limitations: An older specialist diffusion-on-finite-cycle or optimal-coupling computation could have exactly this time-dependent formula under other normalizations.
